Pokemon Showdown, gen 9 random battle, singles. "We" are the side to act; "foe" is the opponent. Turn 10. REQUEST: choose a move or a switch. We can Terastallize this turn (our active's Tera type: Steel).
POKEMON LEFT: ours 6 of 6; the foe's 5 of 6 (2 not seen yet). Our network's win estimate: 75%.
OUR ACTIVE: Goodra L85 (Dragon) HP 47%; item none; ability Sap Sipper; Tera type Steel.
FOE'S ACTIVE: Swalot L90 (Poison) HP 26%; item not shown (likely Leftovers, Assault Vest); ability not shown (possible Liquid Ooze); moves seen: Earthquake, Knock Off; may also have: Gunk Shot, Swords Dance, Protect, Sludge Bomb, Toxic, Clear Smog; can still Terastallize (possible types: Dark, Ground).
SPEED: we move first (ours 185, the foe's about 150).
THREATS: it may carry Swords Dance; its seen moves do up to 29% to our active (Earthquake); a move it may have (Gunk Shot) could do 52%.
FOE'S BENCH (seen so far): Keldeo-Resolute L79 (Water/Fighting) HP 51%, seen: Hydro Pump, Secret Sword, Leftovers; Lokix L82 (Bug/Dark) HP 100%, seen: First Impression. Fainted: Ariados.
FIELD: weather none; our side: nothing; foe's side: nothing.
LAST TURN: our Goodra used Earthquake; foe's Swalot at 26%; foe's Swalot used Knock Off; our Goodra at 47%; our Goodra lost its Assault Vest.
FOE'S LIKELY NEXT ACTION (our model of opponents): Earthquake 20%, Knock Off 16%, Sludge Bomb 15%, something else 48%.
ADVISORS: mix (our network and search together) would play Draco Meteor. The network alone: Draco Meteor (96%). The search alone: Earthquake (31% of its visits).

questions.name: action
questions.instructions: You choose our action in a Pokemon Showdown gen 9 random battle. Pick the action most likely to WIN THE GAME, not only this turn. Each choice lists its facts and two advisors: net = our neural network's probability for that move or switch (it does not judge Terastallizing), search = the share of visits our look-ahead search gave exactly that action, with its average result (0 lost, 1 won). Together ("mix") they play at about 2350 Elo: follow them unless the facts give a concrete reason not to. Respect type immunities and abilities: never pick a move that does nothing. Do not stay in on a boosted sweeper without an answer: knock it out, remove its boosts, force it out, or switch to something that takes its hits. Take a safe knockout when one is there. When ahead, convert the lead safely: no needless risk, no low-accuracy move where a sure one does the job. Do not waste Terastallization, and do not switch without a reason: a switch gives the opponent a free turn.
